verdict.justification: B offers the stronger executive negotiation guide because it converts the continuity requirement into a quantified last-time build, a defined exit date, and clear concession and escalation sequences. Its proposal for approximately 5,200 sets, completed around W10 at ramp capacity or W15 at baseline capacity, gives LiIon a credible alternative to A’s preferred arrangement requiring continuing monthly cooperation for another six to seven months. A also contains a consequential planning error: its Days 14–21 action promises “≈+490 sets at 1,500/month, ≈+1,190 at 2,500,” although those incremental quantities require roughly three weeks, not the one week allocated. B provides stronger execution controls through completion criteria, ramp-confirmation triggers, volume-change sensitivity, and explicit protection against waiving safety-related warranty liability. Both documents sincerely explore LPI’s grievances and appropriately acknowledge the weakness of LiIon’s immediate BATNA, but B more clearly connects the negotiation terms to the operational transition. B still needs validation of its accelerated plastics mould-out and freight assumptions before commitments are made, but its overall strategy is more actionable and commercially disciplined.
